newsitem.title: USA: Social security benefits to rise 2.9 percent in '97.
newsitem.headline: Social security benefits to rise 2.9 percent in '97.

text.p: Social Security recipients will receive a 2.9 percent cost-of-living increase in their benefit payments next year, the Social Security Administration said Wednesday.
The increase, which will be payable starting Jan. 3, 1997, will increase the average monthly benefit payment to $745 from $724, it said.

Social Security benefits increase automatically each year based on the rise in consumer prices from the third quarter of one year to the next. Some 44 million elderly people receive Social Security benefits.

Supplemental Security Income benefits will also increase by 2.9 percent in 1997. These benefits are paid to about 6-1/2 million poor people who are elderly or disabled. The maximum monthly benefit under this plan will rise to $484 from $470.

Also going up in 1997 is the maximum earnings level subject to the 7.65 percent social security tax rate. Starting next year, earnings above $65,400 will not be subject to the tax. The maximum this year was $62,700.
